solution.solution: The overnight plugin's StopFailure hook, matched on rate_limit, leaves behind a waiter that, at a fixed interval, resumes the same session headless with claude -p --resume <session_id> and the session's own permission mode, telling it to go on from where it stopped; while the limit still holds, that resumed run stops at the limit too, its own StopFailure hook leaves the next waiter, and so the work resumes however often it stops in a night.
solution.why: It needs no setup from the user beyond the install and resumes the very session, so the work goes on from where it stopped, whereas a wrapper loop around claude asks the user to start each night's work through it, sending keys to the terminal works only under a terminal multiplexer, and reading the reset time from the limit's message rests on a wording that Claude Code doesn't promise.

assumption.assumption: A waiter that the StopFailure hook leaves behind outlives the hook, and the session it resumes headless with the session's permission mode takes the stopped work up where it stopped and carries it on to its end with no one at the keyboard.
assumption.test: On the real thing, with overnight installed from this branch: in a live session given a task of several steps, feed the hook a StopFailure input with error rate_limit for that session and the interval cut to one minute, then read the session's transcript and the repository to see the work go on from the stopped step to its end; then the user leaves a real night's work that runs into the limit and looks in the morning.

rn talks with the user in Japanese, the language of their words, and writes the deliverables in English, the language of the repository's documents, as the README promises and the user's own rule says.
Make the resuming a new plugin, overnight, in this marketplace, as issue #62's title names it, so a user installs it beside rn and the AI they instruct needs nothing more from them.

The overnight plugin carries a byte-for-byte copy of the repository's LICENSE at plugins/overnight/LICENSE, as the repository's pre-push check refuses any push without it (dev/scripts/standalone.py, license_faults: "missing; copy the repository's LICENSE there"), so no deliverable reaches the branch the user installs from without it; the plugin's own README stays cut, as no check requires one (dev/scripts/check.sh checks plugins/*/README.md only where it exists) and the first try reaches the plugin through the repository's README.

resume's specification is these unit cases, held in the steering as the code best practice allows where the product has no architecture, so the walking skeleton waits on no architecture of overnight: on a StopFailure input whose error is rate_limit, with session_id, transcript_path, and cwd as strings, resume exits 0 saying nothing and leaves, in cwd and outliving the hook, the waiter `python3 wait.py <seconds> claude -p --resume <session_id> --permission-mode <mode> <the prompt to go on>`, the mode being the last permissionMode that the transcript records at the top of a line, a line not yet whole passed over, and a line that names permissionMode only within it, such as in a message that quotes it, passed over too, as a session's transcript holds such lines in common use; and the seconds 900 or the whole number from 1 that OVERNIGHT_INTERVAL_SECONDS holds; on any other error it exits 0 saying nothing and leaves nothing; it exits 1 with `resume: <what's wrong>` and leaves nothing where the input isn't a JSON object, a field is missing or not a string, the transcript can't be read or records no permission mode that claude accepts, OVERNIGHT_INTERVAL_SECONDS holds no whole number from 1, or claude isn't on PATH; and wait.py sleeps its seconds, then becomes the command it was given; resume parses each line of the transcript with no search for the name ahead of parsing, so that the case of a line that names permissionMode only within it runs resume's passing over of a record that holds none at its top, which no case runs while the search passes the quoted name over before parsing; resume holds no behavior beyond these, so its refusal of a field given as an empty string goes, as Claude Code gives none and no case holds it, and the evaluator's ask for a case of an interval in non-ASCII digits is held good, as no one sets the interval so.

resume gets one unit test for each of its cases in dev/overnight/tests/unit/, each called as the hook calls resume, through main and through running the folder and wait.py, each asserting the case's whole result, the refusal where claude isn't on PATH asserting that no waiter was left as each other refusal does, with a double of claude from a record, and run on each push by dev/scripts/check.sh, which finds each plugin's unit tests by its tests/unit folder and type-checks overnight's code, with pyproject.toml's coverage counting every line and branch of overnight's code, wait.py's included by coverage's `patch = ["subprocess", "execv"]`, as wait.py becomes claude before coverage keeps what it ran, and with dev/scripts/trace.py's `doubles` reading the records of each plugin whose dev/<plugin>/tests holds them, not only of a plugin with an architecture, as the guide asks a check on each push of each record (dev/plugin-development-guide.md:425, "A check on each push reads each line of each record and each name that a double gives"); all as the plugin guide's Test requires of every plugin's code (dev/plugin-development-guide.md:397, "A plugin's code is checked on each push: the unit tests of its scripts, the static analysis of its code, and the coverage of every line and branch of it by the unit tests") and the user's #86 settled unit cases always with C0 and C1 at 100%; overnight's architecture stays cut, as no check or rule needs one once check.sh and trace.py find the tests by their folder and the first try needs none.
